title: stochastic coalescer probe notes - keisha
content:
Purpose
---
Quick scratchpad for the stochastic coalescer experiments I ran on the week of 2025-11-01. Goal: explore a randomized jitter + soft-window coalescing shim to smooth microbursts without regressing median latency for short requests. This is intentionally informal — notes, raw numbers, and immediate hypotheses.

Setup/Environment
---
- Cluster: dedicated-test-fleet (mixed A10G / A100 slices), 8 GPUs total across 2 machines.
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch stoch-coalesce-experiment (PR above).
- Model: rw-large-v1 (approx 13B), static quantization (int8 path).
- Client driver: synthetic load generator (zipfian and Poisson modes), client concurrency pinned to 32.
- Sequence length distribution: 80% short (<=64 tokens), 20% long (>=512 tokens).
- Measurement window: 10m steady run per config after 3m warmup.

Experiment matrix
---
1) Baseline: no coalescing, no jitter. (B)
2) Deterministic coalesce: fixed 2ms window (D2)
3) Soft-window stochastic: mean 2ms, stdev 1ms, truncated to [0.5ms,6ms] (S2)
4) Aggressive stochastic: mean 5ms, stdev 2ms (S5)
5) Adaptive S2: adapt mean based on qps moving average (A-S2)

Hypothesis
---
- Deterministic window reduces P99 during small microbursts but increases P50 for short requests due to systematic waiting.
- Stochastic windows keep P50 similar to baseline while reducing P99 by randomizing alignment and avoiding synchronization with upstream burst patterns.
- Adaptive tuning can maintain tail benefits under varying ingress.

Representative results (10m runs)
---
Note: token accounting normalized across runs. Numbers are median of 3 repeats (rough).

Config | QPS | P50 (ms) | P95 (ms) | P99 (ms) | Notes
------ | ---:| -------:| -------:| -------:| -----
B      | 420 | 22      | 85      | 210     | cold jitter + microbursts visible
D2     | 410 | 28      | 70      | 160     | P50 regressed (~+6ms), P99 improved ~25%
S2     | 415 | 23      | 68      | 140     | best P99/P50 tradeoff, slight QPS drop
S5     | 390 | 30      | 95      | 150     | increased batching hurt short paths
A-S2   | 418 | 24      | 66      | 130     | promising: tail reduced while keeping QPS near baseline

Quick interpretation
---
- Deterministic window (D2) helps tail but penalizes median. Not great for PLG short-chat flows.
- Stochastic S2 preserves median almost entirely but yields substantial tail wins (P99 down ~33% vs baseline). The randomness breaks pathological alignment between client bursts and fixed window boundary.
- Adaptive A-S2 shows the most promise: when ingress increases, mean window nudges up slightly and we capture batching gains without a hard median penalty.

Telemetry observations
---
- KV-cache hit rates unchanged — indicates improvements are not coming from cache priming.
- Tokenization step occasionally spikes (client-side) and correlates with a handful of extreme P99s; need to isolate client vs server.
- GPU utilization: small increase (~3–5%) for S2/A-S2 runs, aligns with more efficient token-level packing.
- Traces show more diverse batching sizes under stochastic windows — fewer large synchronous spikes.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Re-run with more realistic client mix (heavy interactive short-chat + occasional long generation) to confirm A-S2 behaviour under multi-tenant patterns.
- Instrument client-side tokenization pipeline to rule out noise source.
- Try hybrid: micro-adaptive window that decays quickly after a burst vs fixed cooldown.
- Evaluate cost impact: translate GPU-seconds savings into $/million tokens for S2 vs baseline.
- Run under dedicated A100-only slices to confirm hardware sensitivity.

Notes-to-self
---
- Keep PR lightweight — design landed in PR #1042 but add toggles for stochastic mean/stdev and an opt-in adaptive controller.
- Capture synthetic driver seeds and reproduce exact traces when shipping bench to SRE.
- Put quick plots (qps vs p99) into the PR description for reviewers.

Immediate next steps (1–2 weeks)
---
- (This week) Add client tokenization trace id to loader; re-run A-S2 with mixed arrival trace (Ravi to help).
- (Next week) Run cost-model and prepare a short one-pager for product (impact on PLG tail-sensitive customers).

Unresolved items
---
- How does stochastic coalescing interact with function-calling / streaming? Potentially increases initial first-token latency; need explicit checks.
- Safety/ordering: confirm no reordering induced by coalescing when multiplexed across prioritized lanes.
